transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-06-12
Start: 15:30 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Lucas Martinez (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Parallax Procurement), Omar Siddiqi (Parallax Infosec), Daniel Brooks (Parallax ML Platform), Sofia Alvarez (Parallax Counsel)

Summary:
Quick negotiation session focused on privileged keying (KMS vs Redwood-managed keys), SLA terms for Dedicated capacity, DPA deletion/retention language, and pricing approval thresholds for pilot -> committed capacity. Agreed actions: Redwood to provide redlined MSA/DPA + tech diagram; customer to prioritize legal redlines and confirm timeline for procurement approval.

Topics Covered:
- Privileged access model (BYOK / Customer KMS / HSM)
- SLA specifics: uptime, latency p95/p99, incident response, credits
- DPA: data deletion, logs retention, telemetry used for quality and billing
- Pricing path: pilot discounts, committed reserved capacity, egress fees
- Onboarding timeline and stakeholders (Legal, Procurement, Infosec, ML Platform)

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Lucas Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate you squeezing this in. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Maya Chen: Hi, Maya here.
[00:07] Omar Siddiqi: Omar, Infosec.
[00:09] Daniel Brooks: Daniel from ML platform.
[00:11] Sofia Alvarez: Sofia, legal counsel.
[00:13] Priya Desai: Priya, SE at Redwood.
[00:15] Lucas Martinez: Great. So the goal for today is to go through the MSA/DPA specifics around privileged access and SLA so procurement can have a clear path. I think we sent a baseline earlier — any urgent blockers to call out up front?
[00:29] Maya Chen: Yeah, from procurement perspective timeline is tight — CFO wants a decision by end of month. We need to close pricing and make sure legal agrees to the DPA deletion clause.
[00:38] Sofia Alvarez: Specifically, Parallax is not comfortable with the current data retention language; we were hoping to see explicit deletion guarantees within X days and proof-of-deletion mechanism. Also, scope of telemetry — we need clarity on what telemetry Redwood keeps for performance troubleshooting versus customer data.
[01:02] Priya Desai: Understood. On telemetry we typically separate operational telemetry (metrics, tracing) from customer PII or payloads. Operational traces may be retained for 90 days by default for debugging, but customer can opt to disable detailed request logging — that does impact our ability to debug in some cases.
[01:26] Omar Siddiqi: And KMS — we need BYOK, HSM-backed keys, and a clear key rotation policy. Also, audit logs for key usage must be available to our auditors. How does Redwood manage that with Dedicated vs Private deployments?
[01:42] Priya Desai: For Dedicated/Private we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS or GCP CMEK tied to the VM's services. We also have an HSM integration for on-prem packages. For hosted customers, there is an option for Redwood-managed keys with envelope encryption; but for Parallax given regulated data, BYOK is strongly recommended.
[02:05] Lucas Martinez: So action item — we'll include a KMS pattern diagram showing envelope encryption, where keys live, rotations, and how audit logs surface. Priya will share that.
[02:14] Daniel Brooks: Quick clarification — when you say 'audit logs surface' is that in our console or do you mean logs we pull to our own SIEM? Because we need to ingest to Splunk.
[02:25] Priya Desai: Good question. We can stream audit logs to a customer-owned S3 bucket or push to a syslog endpoint; Splunk forwarders are supported. We'll document common connector patterns.
[02:37] Sofia Alvarez: Back to the DPA — clause 6.3 around derivative data, there's a sentence that looks like it gives Redwood rights to deidentified derivatives. We need to make sure that's scoped only for internal quality and not for productization.
[02:51] Lucas Martinez: Thanks — we can tighten that. The intent is to use de-id aggregates for quality/regression monitoring only, not for resale. We'll propose language: 'aggregate, de-identified metrics used solely to operate and improve the service and not for product development or resale.'
[03:11] Maya Chen: Sounds reasonable but Legal will want it explicit.
[03:14] Sofia Alvarez: Yes please. Also, about SLA — our SREs want p95 generation latency SLOs and credits tied to both availability and latency. The current MSA is availability-only.
[03:28] Priya Desai: We can include latency targets for dedicated capacity; for hosted we have best-effort latency SLAs. For Dedicated we typically commit to 99.9% uptime and p95 latency under X ms for the model family — we can add a table with model classes and corresponding p95 targets.
[03:44] Omar Siddiqi: We're going to require incident response timeline commitments too. E.g., initial acknowledgement within 1 hour, with a dedicated escalation channel and 24/7 support for Sev1. Can Redwood support that?
[03:56] Lucas Martinez: Yes — for enterprise contracts we include 24/7 support and an escalation ladder. We'll put explicit MTR and MTTR expectations and a credit schedule.
[04:06] Daniel Brooks: Pricing — pilot stage: we need pilot credits and a clear conversion path to reserved capacity pricing. Procurement also flagged egress and KMS key usage charges as potential hidden costs.
[04:18] Lucas Martinez: For the pilot we'll propose a time-boxed discounted rate and show an example bill. Egress: we charge standard egress if sending model outputs cross-region, but most inference traffic is small; we'll add examples to the cost worksheet. KMS calls: small per-1M ops fee if you choose Redwood-managed KMS, but with BYOK there is no Redwood KMS fee — only guardian KMS API costs from cloud provider.
[04:42] Maya Chen: Okay, we want the pilot discount and the conversion matrix documented so the finance team can sign off.
[04:50] Sofia Alvarez: Another ask: data residency. Parallax processes EU patient-derived data; the DPA must include hard commitments to process EU data in EU regions and not transfer outside.
[05:02] Priya Desai: We have region controls and can pin model serving to EU-only nodes for Private or Dedicated in our EU region. For hosted we can default to region selection but not guarantee it unless you choose Dedicated or Private — we'll clarify in the SOW.
[05:19] Omar Siddiqi: Can you confirm logging redact features? We need PII redaction in request logs.
[05:25] Priya Desai: Yes — we provide native request redaction patterns and can run customer-side pre-processing plugins to strip PII. There's a trade-off: pre-processing reduces observability. We'll document options.
[05:39] Lucas Martinez: Cool. Let me ask — on the MSA financial terms, procurement asked for net-60 payment terms and an invoice schedule tied to milestone acceptance. Any issues?
[05:50] Maya Chen: Net-60 is preferred; finance will accept net-30 only in specific cases, but we can try to push net-60.
[05:56] Lucas Martinez: We'll flag that and see if Sales Ops can accept net-60 for enterprise customers.
[06:01] Sofia Alvarez: One more legal nuance: indemnity carve-outs — Parallax wants a clause excluding indirect damages for data subject claims. We need to ensure insurance and indemnity buckets align.
[06:12] Lucas Martinez: Understood; we'll propose language and include our standard cyber-insurance details.
[06:17] Daniel Brooks: Timebox on integration: how long to go from pilot to production? Our internal stakeholders want a 6–8 week pilot and then production rollout in 8–12 weeks after sign. Is that feasible?
[06:29] Priya Desai: For a standard POC with integration (SSO, KMS, limited model selection) 6–8 weeks is doable. Dedicated provisioning and any custom on-prem packaging could add lead time — typically 4–6 additional weeks for capacity reservation and keys alignment.
[06:46] Omar Siddiqi: For audit readiness we will require SOC2 Type II and ISO attestation documents. Do you have them ready?
[06:54] Lucas Martinez: Yes — we can share SOC2 Type II report under NDA; ISO cert copies too. We'll include those in the security packet.
[07:02] Maya Chen: Great. Can you also include a sample SOW with milestone acceptance criteria so Finance can map payments?
[07:08] Lucas Martinez: Absolutely. We'll send a sample SOW tied to the pricing worksheet.
[07:12] Sofia Alvarez: On the DPA deletion timeframe: Parallax needs deletion within 7 business days after termination for any customer identifiable logs. Can Redwood commit?
[07:23] Priya Desai: For hosted modes, deletion within 30 days is the standard because of backups and retention. For Dedicated/Private, we can agree to a 7-business-day purge window with a proof-of-deletion report. We'll propose that as an option in the DPA for regulated customers.
[07:40] Omar Siddiqi: That works if we do Dedicated. We'll be pushing for Dedicated due to the residency and KMS needs.
[07:47] Lucas Martinez: Sounds like a path: pilot on dedicated nodes with reserved capacity plan; Redwood to update MSA/DPA with BYOK, 7-day deletion for Dedicated, latency SLAs for p95, incident response times, and a pricing conversion matrix.
[07:59] Daniel Brooks: One last technical: KV cache and state — we need to know where session data resides and how long caches persist, since that affects HIPAA compliance.
[08:10] Priya Desai: Session KV cache is ephemeral by default and stored in encrypted memory on the serving node; we can configure TTLs and not persist to disk for regulated workloads. We'll detail the cache behavior in the tech appendix.
[08:26] Maya Chen: Okay, procurement will also need to see an estimated monthly cost for 10M tokens/month baseline and for 50M tokens/month to compare with other vendors.
[08:36] Lucas Martinez: Priya and I will assemble a cost model with examples and edge-case egress/KMS lines.
[08:42] Sofia Alvarez: Next steps and ownership?
[08:45] Lucas Martinez: I'll summarize: Lucas to circulate redlined MSA and DPA with clarified derivative data language and deletion options by Monday 6/16; Priya to share KMS/keys/architecture diagram and cache appendix by Wednesday 6/18; we'll include SOC2/ISO artifacts under NDA; Finance/Procurement will try to confirm net terms; Parallax legal to provide prioritized redlines by 6/20; schedule a 30-minute legal triage week of 6/23. Any objections?
[09:12] Sofia Alvarez: No objections. Please mark the parts that are negotiable vs non-negotiable in the MSA.
[09:18] Lucas Martinez: Will do — we'll annotate negotiable items.
[09:21] Daniel Brooks: Thanks, everyone.
[09:23] Maya Chen: Thanks.

End of transcript.

Notes and artifacts referenced:
- Baseline MSA/DPA v1 (sent 2025-06-09)
- Pricing worksheet (example bills for 10M / 50M tokens)
- KMS pattern diagram (to be provided)
- SOC2 Type II report (to be shared under NDA)
